semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer m ≥ 2 and every integer g ≥ 0, there exists a function J_{m,g} mapping each x ∈ K_{m,g} (i.e., each positive integer (m−1)-tuple with sum g and satisfying the given conditional inequalities for all i,j∈{1,...,m−1}) into K_{m,g+1} (same constraints but sum g+1), such that for all x,y ∈ K_{m,g}, x ≠ y implies J_{m,g}(x) ≠ J_{m,g}(y).

payload.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2 and let g be an integer with g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i + j < m then x_i + x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then x_i + x_j + 1 >= x_{i+j-m}, and such that x_1 + ... + x_{m-1} = g. Define K_{m,g+1} analogously with coordinate sum g+1. Then there exists an injective function J_{m,g} from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}.

result_payload.proof_summary: I found a natural candidate map: for x in K_{m,g}, increase by 1 a coordinate where x attains its minimum. This does preserve the defining inequalities, because if x_r is minimal then for every defining inequality having x_r on the right-hand side, the left-hand side is at least 2x_r, hence at least x_r+1. However, I could not make this into an injective map: different tuples can map to the same target if one simply increments a chosen minimal coordinate (for example in m=4, the three tuples (1,2,2), (2,1,2), (2,2,1) can all potentially lead toward (2,2,2) under different choices). I also explored choosing the leftmost/rightmost minimal coordinate and the largest feasible coordinate, but I was unable to prove injectivity or construct a canonical inverse. Since I do not have a complete rigorous proof of the existence of an injective map J_{m,g}: K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1} from the tuple conditions alone, I must report failure.

suspected_gaps: I do not have a rigorous injective construction.
I could only verify that incrementing a minimal coordinate preserves membership in K_{m,g+1}, not that one can choose such increments injectively for all source tuples.

result_payload.stuck_point: The key unresolved issue is injectivity. I can show many coordinates are individually incrementable (in particular any coordinate of minimal value), but I could not prove there is a canonical choice yielding an injective global map from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}.
